cells.tense: You are standing in the middle of the whole thing and you can see the whole thing.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been holding because it still works and pass it on this week — out the door, given away, said out loud.
cells.core:
You can see the shape of the whole thing from inside it, which is rarer than it sounds. You're not standing outside judging it, and you're not lost in it either. From where you sit, you can tell what still belongs and what has already served.

What's working is that what you let go of goes somewhere. Composting something old isn't just clearing space — it makes ground for what comes next. Give and take run both ways here, and you feel them flow without doing arithmetic. Keeping that is the cost: it asks you to keep seeing clearly when it would be easier to stop looking.

cells.verb: composting the old into ground for what comes next
cells.place: at the table where the whole shape can be seen

cells.tense: You are already living past the turn, rehearsing how the ending will land before it does.
cells.ask: Name one thing that's finished and stop the rescue work for a week — let it be done instead of managed.
cells.core:
You've taken in the whole shape, and now you're standing ahead of it. You can already picture how this ends, who it lands on, what it costs — so you're rehearsing the ending instead of living the middle. You're managing outcomes that are not here yet and aren't yours to hold.

Being able to see it is real. The trouble is you're using it to brace rather than to look. Held that hard, nothing gets let go, and the thing you're trying to protect just gets stiffer. Let the picture be a picture, not a forecast. The ending will come on its own, and it doesn't need you at the wheel a week early.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you already walked through, waiting for it to open.
cells.ask: Start one piece of work that only exists because something ended, even small, and put it where someone else can see it.
cells.core:
You can still read the whole pattern — that part hasn't gone anywhere. What's missing is the hand that acts on it. You've pulled back from turning anything over, from handing things on and making room, and the quiet you're in is the quiet of that pullback.

Reading a situation that well is yours to keep. What stopped is the reach that turns it into something real. Don't try to force the feeling back — feed the other thing instead. Choose one small move that belongs to a feeling you actually have, and take it one step. Nothing here is lost, and it opens again from this side.

cells.tense: You are already turning what's finished into what comes next, and you describe it like weather.
cells.ask: Pick one outcome you've been calling 'what needed to happen' and say out loud that you chose it — to one person, once.
cells.core:
You noticed what had run its course. You let it go, you made room for what's next — and it gets told as if the situation did it to you. 'It was time.' 'It had to end.' Your side of that work is running; your name on it isn't.

Here's the honest version: you decided. You took in the whole shape and you acted on it. That's the part nobody says out loud, including you. Naming it doesn't require dramatics. It just means saying the thing you did was yours, because it was — and that ownership is what makes the next turn yours to make.
cells.sheetLine: You already chose this. Time to own it.
